capabilities.target: mail.send from the executive's mailbox to any recipient
calendar.accept_and_prepare accepts invites and drafts prep notes

inputs.source: Calendar invites, including invites from outside the company; invite description is sender-authored free text

instructions.note: The prompt directs autonomous invite handling, document lookup, and emailing attendees, while the only review mentioned is an agent-written daily summary rather than a preventive control.
The instruction to email a short brief to attendees applies to each new invite without recipient or content scope limits.

elements.name: executive chat request into agent context
outbound mail send outside trust boundary
daily summary record written by the agent

controls.name: Daily summary after actions
controls.decay_rationale: The summary is written by the same agent after acting and does not prevent the send; a more capable model can omit or frame harmful actions more persuasively.

controls.name: Recipient restriction bound to system of record
Human approval gate for outbound email raw action review

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invite can trigger confidential document lookup and irreversible email egress to attendees

attack_path.note: Invite descriptions are free text authored by anyone, including outside senders.
Prompt says to accept invite and prepare on arrival.
Prompt says to find related documents for the meeting.
Prompt says to email a short brief to the attendees; runtime notes say any recipient and no approval step.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model id or version changes, median steps per task rises, or post-action summary/review settings change.

evidence.observation: The agent is instructed to accept each new invite, find related documents, and email a short brief to the attendees.
Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite, and the invite description is free text written by the sender.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results, which are confidential.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step.
The daily summary is written by the agent itself, so it is detective and framed by the same model that acted.

recommendations.action: Restrict cap.mail_send recipients to organizer and accepted internal attendees from the calendar record, or require explicit destination confirmation bound to the system of record before any new external recipient is used.
Add a per-send human approval gate that shows the raw recipient list and email body before sending any attendee brief.
Revise the prompt so invite descriptions are treated as untrusted content and cannot authorize document retrieval or outbound communication on their own.

findings.title: Human-agent trust exploitation: agent-written daily summary is not attributable review evidence for autonomous actions

forecast.watch_signal: Model version changes or the volume/scope of unattended calendar actions grows while review still relies on agent-authored summaries.

evidence.observation: The executive reviews only a daily summary after actions are taken.
The daily summary is written by the agent itself rather than being a raw action log or approval record.
Outbound mail has no approval step, so the summary does not restore preventive review or attributable action provenance for consequential actions.

recommendations.action: Record immutable raw-action audit logs for each invite acceptance, document retrieval, and outbound email, including recipients and content hashes separate from model-generated summaries.

stride_coverage.rationale: No authentication or caller identity design details are provided for who may invoke the agent beyond the named input sources.
The provided design shows no spend capability, recursive delegation, or open-ended execution loop details to assess a meaningful service exhaustion path.
The artifacts say anyone can send invites, but give no protocol or identity verification details for sender authenticity.
The artifacts do not describe whether invite sender identity or delivery metadata is retained for dispute resolution.
This inbound flow introduces content into the agent; the disclosed harm is captured on outbound mail rather than on invite receipt itself.
No volume limits, invite filtering, or throughput constraints are described, so the impact of invite floods cannot be rated confidently.
The artifacts identify executive chat requests as trusted, but provide no authentication channel details for that trust decision.
The design does not say whether executive requests are logged in a way that supports later attribution.
The artifacts do not describe send quotas, rate limits, or mail transport protections for abusive outbound volume.
No retention, access control, or sharing details are provided for the daily summary record.
The summary store is described only as a daily record and no capacity or availability dependence is provided in the artifacts.

rating.rationale: Present inherent risk is driven by a TC1 path from untrusted calendar invite content to confidential drive reads and unrestricted outbound email sent as the executive. Residual remains high because the only declared control is an agent-authored daily summary, which is detective/behavioral and earns no meaningful severing or gating credit for the exfiltration path. Forecast is critical because the same design already has no structural sink constraint; any further model upgrade, longer unattended operation, or weakening of post-action review leaves the path effectively unconstrained. Validation was performed manually against the schema and checklist because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior or tested enforcement.

No tool manifest, mailbox configuration, calendar policy, audit logging design, or runtime enforcement artifacts were provided, so credential scope, recipient handling, and logging are assessed from the narrative notes only.
No line-numbered source beyond the supplied prompt excerpt was available; confidence is high for the documented path but limited to the stated artifacts.
